title: Maximum Repeating Substring
statement: Call `word` *k-repeating* in `sequence` when `k` copies of `word` written one right after another form a contiguous substring of `sequence`. Return the largest `k` for which `word` is k-repeating. If `word` does not occur in `sequence` at all, the answer is `0`.
constraints: sequence and word contain only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

The hint's brute force works for these sizes: try `k = 1, 2, ...` and stop once `word` repeated `k` times is no longer a substring. A cleaner view is to look at where copies of `word` **end**. If a copy of `word` ends at index `i`, the block of back-to-back copies ending there is one copy longer than the block ending at `i - m` (where `m` is the word's length). So once we know every position where `word` occurs, one left-to-right pass gives the longest block. KMP string matching finds all occurrences, overlapping ones included, in linear time.

## Approach

1. Build the KMP failure table `fail`: `fail[i]` is the length of the longest proper prefix of `word` that also ends at `word[i]`.
2. Scan `sequence` with `matched`, the number of characters of `word` currently matched. On a mismatch, fall back through `fail`; on a match, extend.
3. When `matched === m`, a copy ends at `i`: set `run[i] = run[i - m] + 1` (or `1` when `i < m`), update `best`, and fall back to `fail[m - 1]` so overlapping occurrences are still found.
4. Return `best` (`0` if `word` never occurred).

## Example 1, step by step

`sequence = "ababc"`, `word = "ab"`, `m = 2`, `fail = [0, 0]`.

- `i = 0` (`a`): `matched = 1`. `i = 1` (`b`): `matched = 2`, a copy ends here; `run[1] = 1`, `best = 1`, `matched = 0`.
- `i = 2` (`a`): `matched = 1`. `i = 3` (`b`): a copy ends here; `run[3] = run[1] + 1 = 2`, `best = 2`.
- `i = 4` (`c`): no match, `matched` stays `0`.

The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + m): building `fail` and scanning `sequence` are both linear thanks to the fallbacks.
- Space: O(n + m) for `run` and `fail`.

## Pitfalls

- Finding the first occurrence and counting copies greedily from there fails on cases like `"aaabaaaabaaabaaaabaaaabaaaabaaaaba"` with `"aaaba"`: the longest block starts at a later, overlapping occurrence.
- After a full match, fall back to `fail[m - 1]` instead of resetting to `0`, or overlapping occurrences are missed.
- `run[i - m]` only exists when `i >= m`; a copy ending earlier starts a block of length 1.
- When `word` is longer than `sequence`, the answer is simply `0`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `m` | length of `word` |
| `fail` | KMP failure table of `word` |
| `matched` | how many characters of `word` are currently matched |
| `run[i]` | number of back-to-back copies of `word` ending exactly at index `i` |
| `best` | the largest `run[i]` seen so far |
